proof_summary: Quadratic reciprocity makes \(5\) a square modulo \(p\); choosing the larger of the two square roots and setting \(n=s-1\) gives \(p\mid n^2+2n-4\) while ensuring the needed size bounds. Writing \(n^2+2n-4=pc\), recurrence identities express the continued fraction as \(U_2/U_3\) with \(U_2=n^2+2n-4\), show \(c\mid U_3\) via \(c\le n-3\) and a factorial formula for \(U_3\), and show \(p\nmid U_3\), so reduction leaves numerator exactly \(p\); the lone small case \(p=11\) is computed directly.
